title: Cloud networking: VPCs, subnets and load balancers
problem: Every server has a public address, the database answers the internet, and the one NAT gateway in zone a takes the whole fleet offline when that zone fails.
summary: A VPC is your own address space in a region, split into public and private subnets per zone. Internet and NAT gateways decide who reaches out, security groups and network ACLs decide who gets in, and endpoints keep AWS traffic off the metered path.
catTip: The front door is for visitors. The cat flap is for me going out, and it counts every trip and charges the humans per squeeze. I asked for one flap per room so a stuck door never traps the whole house. Granted, reluctantly.

recall.q: What makes a subnet public, and what do private subnets use to reach the internet?
recall.a: A subnet is public when its route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway. Private subnets route outbound traffic to a NAT gateway in a public subnet, which is zonal and charges per gigabyte, so you want one per zone and gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB.

guide.breaks: Without private subnets and stateful security groups every server is reachable from the internet, and a single-zone NAT gateway or a stateless rule that forgets ephemeral ports cuts off whole tiers at once.
guide.tradeoffs: Private subnets need NAT gateways that are zonal and charge per gigabyte, PrivateLink endpoints cost per hour per zone, and every extra boundary is another route table and rule set to get wrong.
guide.explainSimply: A VPC is an office building you design: reception lets visitors into the lobby floors only, the mail room sends parcels out from the private floors but accepts none in, and each door lock remembers who it let through. You build one mail room per wing so a flood does not stop the whole building's post.
guide.hint: Think about which route makes a subnet public, and what the private ones use instead.

meow: Public subnet: door to the street. Private subnet: cat flap through NAT, metered per squeeze, one per zone. Security group remembers me, network ACL does not.

quiz.prompt: App servers in private subnets across three zones all route 0.0.0.0/0 to a single NAT gateway in zone a. What is the design flaw?
options: Private subnets cannot use a NAT gateway; they need an internet gateway of their own
If zone a fails, servers in zones b and c lose outbound internet access, and their traffic to the NAT gateway crosses zones
A NAT gateway can serve only the subnet it is created in
Security groups will block the return traffic, because NAT is stateless
quiz.explanation: A NAT gateway is zonal, so AWS recommends one per zone with zone-local routes. The last option is the tempting error: both the NAT gateway and security groups are stateful, so return traffic is allowed; it is network ACLs that are stateless.

quiz.prompt: Which pair correctly contrasts security groups and network ACLs?
options: Security groups are stateless and ordered; network ACLs are stateful and allow-only
Security groups apply to subnets; network ACLs apply to individual instances
Security groups are stateful with allow rules only, evaluated as a set; network ACLs are stateless with allow and deny rules, evaluated in number order
Both are stateful, but only network ACLs support deny rules
quiz.explanation: That is AWS's own comparison: instance-level, stateful, allow-only and all-rules versus subnet-level, stateless, allow-and-deny and first-match. The last option is half right about deny rules, but network ACLs are stateless, which is why return traffic needs explicit ephemeral-port rules.

cards.q: Your app servers upload 10 TB a month to S3 through a NAT gateway. What costs you money unnecessarily, and what fixes it?
cards.a: The NAT gateway's per-gigabyte processing charge, about $0.045 per GB in US East, so roughly $450 a month, on traffic that never needed to leave AWS. A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 is free and keeps the traffic private.

cards.q: You must expose an internal payments API to a partner's VPC without peering, and your address ranges overlap. Which construct do you use?
cards.a: A PrivateLink endpoint service: put the API behind a Network Load Balancer, publish it as an endpoint service, and the partner creates an interface endpoint in their VPC that receives a private address in their own range.

glossary.note: A software-defined private network inside a cloud region with its own address range, subnets, route tables and gateways.
Rewriting private source addresses to a shared public one on the way out; a NAT gateway does it for private subnets, zonally and per gigabyte.
The address-plus-prefix notation such as 10.0.0.0/16 used to size VPCs and subnets.
A stateless, numbered allow-and-deny filter attached to a subnet, evaluated in order until a rule matches.
AWS's layer-7 load balancer for HTTP, HTTPS and gRPC, routing by host, path, header, method, query string or source address.
AWS's layer-4 load balancer for TCP, UDP and TLS with a static address per zone and the client's source address preserved.

sources.title: Amazon VPC User Guide, NAT gateway basics
sources.supports: a NAT gateway is created in one Availability Zone; if that zone is down, resources in other zones lose internet access, so create one per zone; 5 Gbps scaling to 100 Gbps; 55,000 simultaneous connections per unique destination per address

sources.title: Amazon VPC User Guide, NAT gateways
sources.supports: public NAT gateways sit in a public subnet and give private instances outbound internet access

sources.title: Amazon VPC pricing
sources.supports: NAT gateway charges of $0.045 per hour and $0.045 per GB processed in US East, plus standard data transfer

sources.title: Amazon VPC User Guide, Security groups
sources.supports: security groups are stateful, allow rules only; a new group has no inbound rules and allows all outbound

sources.title: Amazon VPC User Guide, Security group rules
sources.supports: rules can reference another security group as the source

sources.title: Amazon VPC User Guide, Network ACLs
sources.supports: network ACLs are stateless, have numbered allow and deny rules evaluated from the lowest number with first match applied, and need ephemeral-port rules (1024 to 65535) for return traffic

sources.title: Amazon VPC User Guide, Default and custom network ACLs
sources.supports: the default network ACL allows all traffic; a custom one denies everything until rules are added
